claim: `sign_nostr_identity_binding` is the only signing command in identity.rs that reads `state.keys.lock()` directly instead of `state.signing_keys()`, so it bypasses the recovery-mode gate that refuses signing when `identity_lost` or `keyring_locked` is set. The same path also lets the ephemeral key be bound while `keyring_locked`, i.e. while the user's real key still exists but is unreachable.

votes.reasoning: The quoted config value is real (desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:38-40, and the only other config file, src-tauri/tauri.dev.conf.json, sets just identifier/productName), but `csp: null` is Tauri's default "do not inject a CSP" setting, not an override that turns off a protection that would otherwise be active. Under a reachability lens the finding has no attacker-to-failure path: it is entirely conditional on "if any renderer path fails to escape relay-supplied content", and the reporter did not identify such a path. I looked for one. Relay-supplied message bodies are rendered through react-markdown called as a plain function in desktop/src/shared/ui/markdown/nodeCache.ts:83-109; the rehype plugin list is `[rehypeImageGallery]` plus an optional search-highlight plugin (nodeCache.ts:86-89) — there is no `rehype-raw` and no `allowDangerousHtml`, so raw HTML in relay content is not parsed into elements, and `urlTransform: messageLinkUrlTransform` is applied to link/image URLs. A repo-wide grep for raw-HTML sinks in desktop/src returns exactly two hits: desktop/src/features/messages/ui/BotIdenticon.tsx:31, whose `__html` comes from `jdenticon.toSvg(value, size)` (BotIdenticon.tsx:23) — a hash-derived SVG that does not echo its input — and desktop/src/features/messages/lib/normalizeMentionClipboard.ts:49, which reads `doc.body.innerHTML` rather than writing it. With no injection sink, there is no control flow from a remote peer's event content to script execution, so the described failure cannot occur in a shipped build. Adding a restrictive CSP remains a reasonable defense-in-depth recommendation, but it is a hardening suggestion, not a reachable vulnerability, and the claimed 'high' rests on a hypothetical bug the reporter did not find.

The factual half of the claim checks out and I could not refute it: `app.security.csp` is literally `null` (desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:38-40), and there is no substitute CSP meta tag in desktop/index.html and no CSP header set anywhere in src-tauri, so Tauri injects no policy. What I refute is the 'high' rating and the implied XSS exposure. The sink the finding assumes is not there: relay content is rendered through react-markdown (desktop/src/shared/ui/markdown/nodeCache.ts:94-109) with remark/rehype plugins only - rehype-raw is NOT in the plugin list, so raw HTML in message bodies is escaped, not parsed; link hrefs go through messageLinkUrlTransform (desktop/src/shared/ui/markdown/utils.ts:174-179) which falls through to react-markdown's defaultUrlTransform, blocking javascript:/data: hrefs; and the single `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in the app (desktop/src/features/messages/ui/BotIdenticon.tsx:31) is fed jdenticon's `toSvg(value, size)` output, which hashes `value` rather than embedding it. So the CSP gap is a defense-in-depth omission worth fixing (a one-line config change), not a high-severity vulnerability: there is no first-stage injection for it to mitigate.

claim: `get_channels` swallows relay errors on both of its enrichment queries with `.unwrap_or_default()` (member counts at line 221, last-message timestamps at line 252). A transient relay failure on either query is indistinguishable from 'this data is genuinely empty': the command still returns `Ok` with every channel reporting zero members and no last-message timestamp.
failure_scenario: The relay returns a 5xx (or the HTTP call times out) on the batched kind:39002 query during a channel-list refresh. `query_relay(...).await.unwrap_or_default()` yields an empty Vec, `collect_members_by_channel` produces an empty map, and the `if let Some(info)` at line 225 never fires — so `member_count` stays at whatever `channel_info_from_event` defaulted it to (0) for every channel. The same failure on the per-channel last-message filters at line 252 leaves `last_message_at` as `None` everywhere. The user sees their entire channel list report '0 members' and lose its recency ordering, with no error banner and nothing in the UI to distinguish it from a real empty workspace — the natural reaction is to think the workspace was wiped.

votes.reasoning: Confirmed mechanically, downgraded to low: it is a transient display-degradation issue, not a security or data-integrity problem. Verified: get_channels (channels.rs:79, registered lib.rs:744) propagates errors from its primary queries with `?` (channels.rs:92, :136, :147), but both enrichment queries swallow failures — the batched kind:39002 member-count query at channels.rs:212-221 ends in `.await.unwrap_or_default()`, and the per-channel last-message query at channels.rs:252 does the same. query_relay is a real HTTP POST to the relay (desktop/src-tauri/src/relay.rs:315-341) that returns Err on network failure or non-2xx, so a mid-command transient failure yields Ok with member_count left at the 0 default (the comment at channels.rs:204-209 confirms 0 is what channel_info_from_event produces without this step) and last_message_at None. So the described state is reachable. Severity correction rationale: it requires the relay to succeed on the first three queries and fail moments later within the same command invocation (a whole-relay outage errors the command normally); the channel list is refetched periodically so the state self-heals on the next successful poll; nothing is persisted; and no trust boundary is crossed — the reporter's 'user thinks the workspace was wiped' is a worst-case UX reading of a transient render.
